title: Earthworm — Excretory, Nervous and Reproductive Systems
topicTitle: Earthworm: Excretory system (types of nephridia, structure and arrangement of septal nephridia); nervous system (central and peripheral, working mechanism); reproductive systems (male and female reproductive organs), copulation, cocoon formation and economic importance

The excretory organs of earthworms are called:

notes: Digestive system: buccal cavity → pharynx → oesophagus → crop (storage) → gizzard (grinding) → intestine (with typhlosole for increased surface) → rectum → anus.
Nervous system: cerebral ganglion (brain) above the oesophagus; ventral nerve cord (double sub-oesophageal ganglion) with segmental ganglia; sensory organs in prostomium.
Excretory system: metanephridia (nephridia) — one pair per segment; types: integmentary (perivisceral), septal, and genital; collect coelomic fluid and excrete ammonia/urea.
Circulatory system: closed; dorsal vessel (collects blood), ventral vessel (delivers), 5–6 pairs of heart-like vessels (anterior); coelomic fluid + blood.

Reproductive system: hermaphrodite; male (testes, vasa deferentia, seminal vesicles, sperm duct) and female (ovaries, oviduct, ova); clitellum forms the cocoon; cross-fertilisation via exchange of sperm in a copulatory loop.
Economic importance: soil aeration, humus, decomposition; used in bioremediation; indicator of soil health.
NEB focus: excretory, nervous, and reproductive systems; copulation and cocoon formation.
confusion: Earthworms have a CLOSED circulatory system (blood in vessels), not open.
The crop STORES food; the gizzard GRINDS it (like a chicken's gizzard) — they are different organs.
Nephridia types: intersegmentary (perivisceral) connect two segments; septal are at septa; genital in the clitellum region.
Earthworms are hermaphrodites but STILL cross-fertilise (exchange sperm with a partner).
The ventral nerve cord is the main nerve structure; the cerebral ganglion (brain) is above the oesophagus.
Excretion: earthworms excrete ammonia (urea) in moist environments; they do NOT produce urea like mammals in large amounts.

enrichedContent.summary: The earthworm's internal systems are well adapted to its soil-dwelling life. The digestive system (buccal cavity → crop → gizzard → intestine with typhlosole) processes decaying matter. The closed circulatory system has 5–6 heart-like vessels. The excretory system uses metanephridia (intersegmentary, septal, genital). The nervous system (cerebral ganglion + ventral nerve cord) coordinates peristaltic movement. Reproduction is hermaphroditic with cross-fertilisation and cocoon formation by the clitellum. Earthworms are ecologically and agriculturally important.
